brief.headline: The price of aluminium fell but the premium for metal available today rose sharply - the first time in this run the two have moved in opposite directions, which makes the tightness signal much harder to dismiss as momentum, even as the physical market in Asia looks weaker than it has all quarter.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. The exchange settled aluminium cash at $3,343.00 a tonne on Thursday, down $9.00 or 0.27%, ending three sessions of gains. Three-month fell more than twice as far, down $20.00 to $3,318.00. Because the back of the curve was sold harder than the front, the premium for metal today over metal in three months - the backwardation - WIDENED FROM $14.00 TO $25.00, the widest since 04-August and the fourth consecutive session it has widened.

WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE PRICE. On each of the three previous sessions the price and the spread rose together, which left open an unflattering explanation: that the spread was simply being dragged along by a rising price. Today the price fell and the spread widened anyway. A market selling the forward while bidding the prompt is one losing confidence in the future without losing its need for metal now. Aluminium was also the only metal on the exchange board whose backwardation widened - copper's narrowed sharply and zinc's narrowed slightly - so the signal is aluminium's own again rather than a general move.

THE UNCOMFORTABLE OTHER HALF. The physical market outside the exchange looks weak, and it got weaker on dated evidence this morning. A market review published today puts the consensus for the next quarterly Japanese premium at $280-290 a tonne, below the $310-325 producers themselves opened at and far below the current quarter's record $395. The same review describes premiums falling across Japan, the United States, Vietnam, South Korea and Thailand - and describes Middle Eastern and Australian metal reaching Japan as relatively ample, which is not what a genuine Gulf shortage looks like.

WHAT TO WATCH. Three things, in order. Whether the backwardation holds above $14.00 now that it has widened against the price - that is the test of whether this is physical demand or positioning. Whether the Japanese quarterly premium settles near $280-290, which would confirm that physical Asia is much looser than the London curve implies. And the Middle East, where the week brought both a serious escalation - ships attacked near the Strait of Hormuz, a second chokepoint now threatened at Bab el-Mandeb, oil trading near $110 - and, late in the day, an unconfirmed report that Iran and Oman are seeking a deal over Hormuz. That last item is the one that could change the picture fastest.

kpis.label: LME Cash settlement
kpis.note: FRIDAY 11-SEPTEMBER COMPILE, TAKEN BEFORE THE LONDON RING; TODAY'S OWN OFFICIAL PRINTS AT 13:20 LONDON. THE BOARD PUBLISHED THIS MORNING IS THE 10-SEPTEMBER-2026 OFFICIAL AND THE WHOLE PAGE SITS ON THAT ONE UNIFORM SESSION. THE SOURCE STATE IS CLEAN FOR A THIRD CONSECUTIVE RUN. The English overview and the German overview, each requested with its own cache-busting query string, both carry the 10-SEPTEMBER-2026 board and agree line for line across all six metals, all six warehouse lines and all three EUR/USD fixings. THE ALUMINIUM AND COPPER PER-METAL DAILY TABLES WERE ALSO PULLED AND BOTH CARRY 10-SEPTEMBER AND REPRODUCE THE OVERVIEW EXACTLY; the nickel, zinc and lead rows rest on the two agreeing overview presentations rather than on a third per-metal check, and that narrower verification is stated rather than implied. THE STOCK IDENTITY BALANCES FIVE OUT OF FIVE TO THE TONNE against the prior session plus published changes: copper 235,825 less 1,075 equals 234,750; lead 384,450 less 2,075 equals 382,375; zinc 115,675 less 4,325 equals 111,350; aluminium 244,525 less 175 equals 244,350; nickel 270,924 plus 576 equals 271,500. No row required arithmetic reconciliation. CASH $3,343.00 IS THE 10-SEPTEMBER OFFICIAL, DOWN $9.00 OR -0.27% ON WEDNESDAY'S $3,352.00. THAT ENDS A THREE-SESSION WINNING RUN, AND IT IS REPORTED AS A DECLINE RATHER THAN DRESSED UP AS CONSOLIDATION. THE MORE IMPORTANT FACT IS WHAT THE FRONT OF THE CURVE DID WHILE THE PRICE FELL: three-month fell $20.00 against cash's $9.00, so the BACKWARDATION WIDENED FROM $14.00 TO $25.00. FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS SEQUENCE THE FLAT PRICE AND THE SPREAD MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, and that is a materially stronger tightness signal than the three sessions before it, because a widening backwardation on a falling price cannot be explained as flat-price momentum dragging the front along with it. THE LEVEL IS STILL RESPECTABLE AND THE LIMITS ARE STATED: $3,343.00 remains the second-highest cash settlement since 11-August, it is still $15.50 above the 10-August high of $3,327.50 that the four-week range was defined by, and the range top therefore remains cleared. It is $30.00 below the 11-August settlement of $3,373.00 and $512.00 below the 02-June high of $3,855.00. Across the four sessions from Friday's $3,292.50 the metal is still up $50.50, or 1.53%.

kpis.label: LME 3-month
kpis.note: THREE-MONTH SETTLED $3,318.00 ON 10-SEPTEMBER, DOWN $20.00 OR -0.60%, MORE THAN TWICE THE FALL IN CASH. THAT $11.00 DIFFERENCE IS THE ENTIRE STORY OF THE SESSION: the back of the curve was sold harder than the front, which is what widened the backwardation to $25.00. A MARKET LETTING GO OF THE FORWARD WHILE HOLDING THE PROMPT IS ONE THAT IS LOSING CONVICTION ABOUT THE FUTURE WITHOUT LOSING ITS NEED FOR METAL NOW. That is a narrower, more physical bull case than the one the page carried yesterday, and it is a less comfortable one for anybody positioned for a trend. THE THREE-MONTH IS THE CONTRACT THE FORWARD MODEL AND THE ELLIOTT WAVE COUNT ARE ANCHORED ON. At $3,318.00 it sits $56.00 below the 11-August impulse high of $3,374.00, which remains the cleanest published upside trigger on the technical panel, and $135.00 above the 20-August low of $3,183.00 that is the published invalidation.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: CASH SETTLED $25.00 ABOVE THREE-MONTH - A BACKWARDATION, AND THE CONVENTION IS STATED EXPLICITLY BECAUSE THE SIGN MATTERS: cash above three-month is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt tightness; cash below is CONTANGO. THE SPREAD WIDENED FROM $14.00 TO $25.00 AND IS THE WIDEST BACKWARDATION SINCE 04-AUGUST, when it printed $34.50. It has now widened on FOUR consecutive sessions from a $0.50 contango on 04-September, through $2.00, $6.00 and $14.00, to $25.00. THIS IS THE DIVERGENCE THE PAGE HAS BEEN WAITING FOR AND IT IS FLAGGED EXPLICITLY AS THE CONVENTION REQUIRES: SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS TODAY. The price fell and the premium for prompt metal rose. On the three prior sessions both rose together, which left open the reading that the spread was simply following the price; that reading is no longer available. THE SCALE CAVEAT IS KEPT IN PLACE AND IT IS NOT A FORMALITY, BUT IT HAS LOOSENED: $25.00 on a $3,343 metal is seventy-five hundredths of one percent, against forty-two hundredths yesterday. It is still well short of the 3.61% zinc is paying on the same board. THE AUGUST AVERAGE SPREAD WAS A $1.60 CONTANGO, so the current print is more than twenty-six dollars clear of the month it followed. THE CROSS-METAL COMPARISON HAS FLIPPED BACK IN ALUMINIUM'S FAVOUR: of the three backwardated metals on this board, aluminium is the ONLY one whose backwardation widened. Copper's narrowed from $40.00 to $19.00 and zinc's from $150.00 to $143.00.

kpis.label: LME stocks (t)
kpis.note: EXCHANGE STOCK FELL 175 TONNES TO 244,350 ON 10-SEPTEMBER. THE HEADLINE IS THAT THE SERIES MOVED AT ALL: it had printed a published change of exactly ZERO for three consecutive sessions and had shown the identical number on four consecutive readings back to 04-September. THAT STANDSTILL IS BROKEN, AND 244,350 IS A FRESH LOW FOR THE SERIES. THE SIZE OF THE MOVE IS STATED HONESTLY AND IT IS TRIVIAL: 175 tonnes is seven hundredths of one percent of the stock and is a rounding error against a 244,350-tonne total. This is a series resuming a pulse, not a warehouse being drained. ACROSS THE FIFTEEN SESSIONS FROM 20-AUGUST TO 10-SEPTEMBER STOCK HAS FALLEN 2,575 TONNES, ABOUT 172 TONNES A SESSION, AND ALL BUT 175 OF THAT HAPPENED BEFORE 04-SEPTEMBER. THE HONEST READ IS UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE: the thirty-six-year low is real and is the strongest single support under the price, but the draw that produced it has all but stopped. WHAT MAKES THIS SESSION INSTRUCTIVE IS THAT THE CURVE TIGHTENED SHARPLY WHILE THE WAREHOUSE BARELY MOVED AND WHILE THE PRICE FELL - direct evidence that prompt demand can firm without the inventory series registering it, and the third distinct piece of evidence for that proposition in a week. THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE IS CARRIED FOR BALANCE AND IT GREW TODAY: Japanese inventories at three major ports were reported down 8.8% month on month to 201,000 tonnes and Shanghai inventories down 3% week on week, so the visible off-exchange series are drawing faster than London's.

kpis.label: EUR/USD (LME FX fixing)
kpis.note: THE LME FX FIXING FELL TO 1.16170 FROM 1.16460 AND THE ECB FIXING FELL FURTHER, TO 1.16160 FROM 1.16520. THE EURO WEAKENED ON THE DAY THE EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK RAISED RATES, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE NAIVE EXPECTATION AND IS WORTH EXPLAINING RATHER THAN GLOSSING. The ECB delivered the fully-priced 25 basis points unanimously, lifting the deposit rate to 2.50%, the main refinancing rate to 2.65% and the marginal lending facility to 2.90%, and Christine Lagarde called the decision a 'no-brainer'. Because the move was fully priced, the currency traded the guidance, and the Governing Council declined to pre-commit to a further step. THE MARKET NONETHELESS PRICED MORE TIGHTENING AHEAD - roughly 88 basis points in total, peaking in September 2027 - so the euro fell on the absence of an explicit commitment rather than on a dovish outcome. A WEAKER EURO MAKES A DOLLAR-PRICED METAL MORE EXPENSIVE FOR A EUROPEAN BUYER AND MARGINALLY BETTER IN EURO TERMS FOR A EUROPEAN SMELTER'S REVENUE LINE - the exact reverse of yesterday, and a small offset to the region's rising energy cost rather than an addition to it. THE BFIX REFERENCE RATE MOVED THIS TIME, to 1.16187 from 1.16450, so all three fixings rolled together and the static-BFIX anomaly of the last two sessions has cleared.

lme.commentary: THE 10-SEPTEMBER SESSION IS THE MOST INFORMATIVE OF THE LAST FORTNIGHT AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN DIRECTIONAL. CASH FELL $9.00 TO $3,343.00 AND THREE-MONTH FELL $20.00 TO $3,318.00, SO THE BACKWARDATION WIDENED FROM $14.00 TO $25.00 - THE WIDEST SINCE 04-AUGUST AND THE FOURTH CONSECUTIVE SESSION OF WIDENING. THE CONVENTION IS STATED BECAUSE THE SIGN CARRIES THE MEANING: cash above three-month is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt tightness; cash below is CONTANGO. AND THE DIVERGENCE IS CALLED OUT EXPLICITLY AS THE CONVENTION REQUIRES - SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS TODAY. THAT IS WHAT MAKES THIS SESSION DIFFERENT FROM THE THREE BEFORE IT. On 07, 08 and 09-September both the price and the spread rose, and a fair sceptic could say the front was simply being carried along by a rising market. A widening backwardation on a FALLING price cannot be explained that way. What it describes is a market that sold the forward harder than the prompt: letting go of a view about the future without letting go of the need for metal now. THE PAGE ALSO RECOVERS AN ARGUMENT IT WITHDREW YESTERDAY, AND SAYS SO RATHER THAN QUIETLY RESTORING IT. Yesterday four of five metals tightened together, so aluminium's move was corroborated by the complex rather than distinguished from it, and this page downgraded the reading accordingly. TODAY THE COMPLEX SPLIT: of the three backwardated metals, aluminium ALONE widened. Copper's backwardation collapsed from $40.00 to $19.00 as cash fell $282.00, and zinc's eased from $150.00 to $143.00. Nickel's and lead's contangos narrowed modestly. All five three-month prices fell. THE WAREHOUSE STILL WILL NOT COOPERATE AND THE PAGE DOES NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE. Stock fell 175 tonnes to 244,350 - the first non-zero print in four readings, a fresh series low, and a rounding error. On the same board lead drew 2,075 tonnes and zinc 4,325. Aluminium has the lowest relative inventory of the five and the smallest draw. THE BROADER SESSION WAS MACRO-DRIVEN AND THAT CONTEXT MATTERS FOR HOW MUCH WEIGHT THE CURVE SIGNAL DESERVES: a hot US producer-price print lifted September Fed hike odds to roughly 70% and pushed the ten-year toward 4.93%, the dollar firmed, the ECB raised rates, and every base metal fell. Aluminium fell LESS than copper or zinc and its curve tightened while theirs loosened. That is a relative-strength observation, and it is offered as one rather than as a forecast.

TWO READINGS REMAIN LIVE AND THE ASSESSMENT CADENCE IS TOO SLOW TO DISTINGUISH THEM: either replacement units are already sourced and the ban is priced, or the event is not in the price at all.

THE ROW SITS ABOVE ITS OWN TRAILING AVERAGE OF $1,144, which is the one European premium line still carrying a firm tone, and it is a value-added billet premium rather than a primary-ingot premium, so it should not be read as a contradiction of the soft duty-unpaid print.

CARRIED AT ITS LAST DATED PUBLIC ASSESSMENT. THE ASSESSMENT DID NOT MOVE; THE DECOMPOSITION DID, BECAUSE THE BENCHMARK MOVED. At a re-verified 50% Section 232 rate on today's $3,343.00 cash settlement the arithmetic tariff leg is $1,671.50, leaving an implied market leg of $422.50 - UP $4.50 from yesterday's $418.00 purely because the exchange price FELL while the assessment stood still. THE DIRECTION OF THAT CHANGE IS A MECHANICAL ARTEFACT AND IS LABELLED AS ONE: nothing was reassessed. THE REAL NEWS FOR THIS ROW IS BEARISH AND IT IS DATED: the 11-September SMM review reports only scattered spot deals in the US primary market, lacklustre physical consumption on the downstream seasonal off-season, spot prices extending losses, regional premiums under pressure AND NO CLEAR SIGN OF STABILIZATION. That is direct evidence AGAINST the mechanical expectation that Canada's counter-tariffs would support US delivered premiums, three full days after they took effect.

THE DUTY-PAID MATCH ROW. Of $2,094/t, $1,671.50 is the arithmetic tariff leg at a verified 50% rate on the 10-September cash settlement of $3,343.00, leaving $422.50 as the implied market leg. THE TARIFF LEG IS RECOMPUTED EVERY RUN; THE ASSESSMENT ITSELF IS PERIODIC AND UNCHANGED. US PREMIUMS ARE TARIFF-INFLATED BY CONSTRUCTION AND THE SPLIT IS SHOWN SO THAT THE POLICY COMPONENT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR A MARKET SIGNAL. The 11-September SMM review reports US regional premiums under pressure with no sign of stabilization, which argues the market leg is more likely to fall than rise at the next dated assessment.

drivers.text: THE PENDING ASIAN QUARTERLY SETTLEMENT FINALLY HAS A DATED CONSENSUS NUMBER, AND IT IS BELOW THE PRODUCERS' OWN OFFER FLOOR — For eight consecutive runs this panel carried a pending Q4 range built only on the 02-September producer offer of $310-325/t and the reported Japanese buyer target of below $300. A dated SMM review published 11-September-2026 now puts the MARKET CONSENSUS at USD 280-290/t and reports that South Korean and Thai traders have already repriced offers toward that band. THE RANGE ON THIS PAGE HAS BEEN NARROWED AND SHIFTED TO $280-310 ACCORDINGLY - the first change in nine runs. The significance is not the arithmetic but the direction of travel: the consensus has moved BELOW the level at which producers opened, which means the burden of concession now sits with the sellers. Against a Q3 record of $395 a settlement at $285 would be a fall of roughly 28% in a single quarter.
drivers.source: Shanghai Metals Market (SMM), 11-September-2026 - market consensus for the upcoming MJP settlement at USD 280-290/t; Korean and Thai traders repricing toward that band

drivers.text: THE US PREMIUM IS FALLING DESPITE A TARIFF WALL ON BOTH SIDES OF THE BORDER, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE MECHANICAL EXPECTATION — Canada's counter-tariffs took effect on 08-September, raising Canadian counter-tariffs on US steel and aluminium from 25% to 50% across $27.6 billion of imports and more than 300 metals products; US Section 232 was re-verified this run at 50% on articles and 25% on derivative articles. The mechanical expectation was support for regional delivered premiums on both sides of a corridor whose volume is suppressed. THREE FULL DAYS IN, THE DATED PUBLIC EVIDENCE POINTS THE OTHER WAY: SMM reports only scattered US spot deals, lacklustre downstream consumption on the seasonal off-season, spot prices extending losses, regional premiums under pressure and NO CLEAR SIGN OF STABILIZATION. THE HONEST READING IS THAT DEMAND IS CURRENTLY BEATING POLICY IN THE US PHYSICAL MARKET. Nothing has been written into the premium rows on the strength of either the policy or this commentary; both await a dated assessment.
drivers.source: Shanghai Metals Market (SMM), 11-September-2026 - US regional premiums under pressure, no clear sign of stabilization

drivers.text: THE TARIFF LEG IS RECOMPUTED EVERY RUN AND IT MOVED TODAY WITHOUT ANY PREMIUM BEING REASSESSED — At a re-verified 50% Section 232 rate on the 10-September cash settlement of $3,343.00, the arithmetic tariff leg of the US Midwest duty-paid row is $1,671.50, leaving an implied market leg of $422.50 out of the carried $2,094/t. That market leg is UP $4.50 on yesterday - not because anything was reassessed, but because the exchange benchmark FELL $9.00 while the assessment stood still. THIS IS DISCLOSED AS A MECHANICAL ARTEFACT RATHER THAN PRESENTED AS A SIGNAL. It is also the clearest illustration on the page of why a tariff-inflated premium is a poor demand indicator: half the number is policy and moves with the benchmark, not with the physical market.
drivers.source: US Section 232 - 50% on aluminium articles, 25% on derivative articles, re-verified this run

drivers.text: THE EUROPEAN DUTY-UNPAID PREMIUM STILL IS NOT BEHAVING AS THOUGH A SCHEDULED SUPPLY SHOCK IS FIFTEEN WEEKS AWAY — Duty-unpaid was last assessed at $485/t, below its own trailing average of $519.10, and the 11-September SMM review describes overseas premiums as broadly soft with demand unlikely to improve materially in the short run. The EU import ban on Russian primary aluminium takes effect 31-December-2026. THE SECOND-ORDER PRESSURE ON THE REPLACEMENT-SUPPLY SIDE INCREASED AGAIN: European gas TTF rose 2.93% to EUR 81.57, a fourth consecutive advance, and the European Central Bank raised rates 25 basis points on 10-September with markets pricing roughly 88 basis points more to come. The region that must absorb a supply shock at year end faces a rising energy cost and a rising policy rate at the same time, which narrows the room for European restarts to supply the replacement units.
drivers.source: Trading Economics cross-asset board read at this compile - European gas TTF EUR 81.57, +2.93%

prices.label: Alumina FOB East Australia (SMM reported trade)
prices.note: REFRESHED THIS RUN WITH A DATED PUBLIC TRADE - THE FIRST NEW MARK ON THIS ROW IN FIVE WEEKS. SMM reports that on 11-September-2026, 50,000 mt of alumina traded at $353.50/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA for October shipment. THE BASIS IS IDENTICAL TO THE MARK IT REPLACES, which is why it was accepted: the row previously carried $356/t from a 05-August trade on the same FOB East Australia basis. The move is DOWN $2.50, or 0.7%, over five weeks - a small decline, and the smallness is the finding. AFTER FIVE WEEKS OF CARRYING A STALE NUMBER AND FLAGGING AN EXPECTED DECLINE, THE MARKET DELIVERED ALMOST NO DECLINE AT ALL. SMM has been publicly guiding that the September monthly average alumina price would fall on surplus, high operating capacity and continued inventory buildup; the first hard print of the month is essentially flat. That is a modest but real disappointment to the falling-cost thesis. A SECOND DATED TRADE ON THE SAME DAY IS CARRIED FOR CONTEXT AND NOT MIXED INTO THIS ROW: 50,000 mt traded at $373/mt FOB INDONESIA for November-2026 shipment, a $19.50 premium to the Australian basis on a later shipment month. AN INTEGRITY CATCH IS RECORDED: an SMM item reporting 30,000 mt at $350/mt FOB WESTERN AUSTRALIA surfaced prominently in search this morning and was REJECTED on two grounds - it carries a publication date of 08-September-2025, making it a prior-year notice, and FOB Western Australia is a different basis from the FOB East Australia series this row maintains. It has not been used. THE STRUCTURAL READ IS OTHERWISE UNCHANGED: the refinery side of the chain remains in surplus while the smelter side is disrupted, and Alunorte has ramped back to full capacity from its August 50% cut on a TEMPORARY terminal-access agreement with its gas supplier.

prices.label: Bauxite (SMM imported index / Guinea CIF China)
prices.note: THE PRICE FIELD IS CARRIED AT ITS LAST DATED PUBLIC MARK AND NOTHING HAS BEEN INTERPOLATED, BUT THE PANEL GAINED A FRESH DATED QUANTITY THIS RUN. SMM's port survey published 11-September-2026 reports that total bauxite inventory at TEN DOMESTIC CHINESE PORTS FELL 1,610,000 TONNES WEEK ON WEEK. THAT IS A LARGE ONE-WEEK DRAW IN THE LEAST-WATCHED AND MOST GEOGRAPHICALLY CONCENTRATED LINK IN THIS CHAIN, and it is the kind of number that tends to be noticed only after it has already moved the alumina price. BAUXITE CARRIES THE MOST CONCENTRATED COUNTRY RISK OF ANY INPUT ON THIS PAGE, with Guinea supply uncertainty the recurring driver of Pacific alumina strength. Because roughly two tonnes of alumina are required per tonne of aluminium, and roughly two to three tonnes of bauxite per tonne of alumina, a bauxite disruption propagates through the whole chain with a lag rather than immediately - which is precisely why it is under-watched relative to its importance. logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: THIS ROW DETERIORATED MATERIALLY AND IT IS THE LARGEST SINGLE CHANGE ON THE PAGE THIS RUN. Public reporting dated 11-September-2026 describes some of the worst fighting of the seven-month conflict: IRAN SAID IT ATTACKED TEN SHIPS NEAR THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ AND THE UNITED STATES SAID IT RETALIATED BY SINKING FIVE IRANIAN TANKERS. A SECOND CHOKEPOINT HAS NOW ENTERED THE PICTURE, WHICH IS NEW: several reports say the Houthi group has seized control of the port city of Mocha and gained leverage over the BAB EL-MANDEB STRAIT, has declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia, has been attacking ships in Bab el-Mandeb and has struck Saudi energy infrastructure. A disruption at Bab el-Mandeb would close an alternative routing that Hormuz-affected cargo has partly relied on. THE PRICE RESPONSE WAS IMMEDIATE: Brent traded as high as $109.97, its highest since early May, and was up roughly 12.4% on the week, its best weekly gain since early July. ONE GENUINELY TWO-SIDED SIGNAL APPEARED LATE IN THE DAY AND IT IS RECORDED WITH ITS UNCERTAINTY ATTACHED RATHER THAN SUPPRESSED: the same publisher's later headline on the same dispatch reported oil REVERSING COURSE AND FALLING ABOUT 1% ON A REPORT THAT IRAN AND OMAN ARE SEEKING A HORMUZ DEAL. That is a single headline on a developing story, it is not a concluded agreement, and it is the FIRST de-escalation signal this row has carried in months. It is flagged because it is the one development that could unwind the largest pillar of the bull case quickly, and it should be treated as unconfirmed until a dated primary announcement exists. THE PHYSICAL CONSEQUENCES REMAIN VISIBLE ACROSS THREE SEPARATE PRODUCERS and are unchanged in substance: EGA publicly at 18% of Al Taweelah capacity, Qatalum curtailed at roughly 60% of a 648,000-tonne nameplate on reduced gas, and Alba with reduction lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March 2026. row.note: EUROPEAN GAS ROSE A FOURTH CONSECUTIVE SESSION, UP 2.93% TO EUR 81.57, AND IS NOW ROUGHLY 11.5% HIGHER ACROSS THE FOUR SESSIONS. This is the single most important row on the page for European smelter economics and for the credibility of the European restart pipeline. IT LANDS ON THE SAME PAGE AS TWO EUROPEAN COMMITMENTS THAT ASSUME WORKABLE POWER ECONOMICS: Slovalco's first 75,000 tonnes of a 175,000-tonne restart guided to Q4-2026 under a Slovak carbon-cost compensation agreement, now roughly three weeks away, and the EU import ban on Russian primary aluminium on 31-December-2026, which Europe must absorb. A RISING GAS PRICE NARROWS THE ROOM FOR EUROPEAN RESTARTS TO SUPPLY THE REPLACEMENT UNITS AT PRECISELY THE MOMENT THOSE UNITS ARE NEEDED, and the European Central Bank raised policy rates into the same conditions on 10-September.

row.label: US dollar index
row.note: THE DOLLAR FIRMED, UP 0.16% TO 98.976, REVERSING YESTERDAY'S SOFTNESS. THE DRIVER IS RATE EXPECTATIONS RATHER THAN RISK APPETITE: a hotter-than-expected US producer-price print on 10-September lifted market-implied odds of a September Federal Reserve rate RISE, which lifted both the dollar and yields. THE CROSS-CURRENT WORTH NOTING IS THAT THE EURO FELL EVEN THOUGH THE ECB RAISED RATES THE SAME DAY, so this is a dollar-strength story rather than a euro-weakness story.

row.label: EUR/USD

The rise to a 2.50% deposit rate was fully priced and delivered unanimously, with Christine Lagarde calling it a 'no-brainer'; the Governing Council declined to pre-commit to a further step, and the currency traded that absence of commitment. MARKETS NONETHELESS MOVED TO PRICE ROUGHLY 88 BASIS POINTS OF FURTHER TIGHTENING WITH A PEAK IN SEPTEMBER 2027, so the hawkish content of the meeting showed up in the rates curve rather than in the exchange rate. FOR THIS INDUSTRY THE PRACTICAL EFFECT IS SMALL AND TWO-SIDED: a weaker euro raises the local-currency cost of dollar-priced metal for a European buyer and marginally improves the euro revenue of a European producer, which is a modest offset to a gas price that rose again on the same session.

row.label: US 10-year Treasury yield
row.note: THE US TEN-YEAR ROSE AGAIN TO 4.880% ON THE REFERENCE BOARD AND REMAINS AT A THREE-YEAR HIGH; SEPARATE REPORTING AROUND THE PRODUCER-PRICE RELEASE PUT IT AS HIGH AS ROUGHLY 4.93%, NEAR THE 5.00% HANDLE, AND BOTH FIGURES ARE SHOWN RATHER THAN THE FLATTERING ONE. THE CAUSE IS DATED AND SPECIFIC: US August producer prices rose 0.4% month on month, in line, BUT 5.4% YEAR ON YEAR, a tenth above expectations, with final-demand goods up 1.1%, energy up 4.2% and diesel alone up 24.1%. Market-implied odds of a September Federal Reserve rate RISE moved to roughly 70%, from about 61% earlier in the week. THE SECOND-ORDER EFFECT ON THIS INDUSTRY IS THE ONE THAT IS USUALLY MISSED AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS: a higher discount rate is a direct headwind for a dollar-priced metal, but it also raises the hurdle rate on every restart and expansion decision in the supply pipeline, which is bullish for the physical balance. THE INFLATION PRINT ITSELF IS ALSO A COST SIGNAL RATHER THAN JUST A POLICY SIGNAL: energy up 4.2% and diesel up 24.1% is freight and power inflation arriving in the producer-price data, which is exactly the cost line a smelter cannot hedge away.

A DATED PUBLIC CONSENSUS FOR THE Q4 JAPANESE PREMIUM FINALLY PRINTED AND IT IS BELOW THE PRODUCERS' OWN OFFER FLOOR. SMM's market review of 11-September-2026 puts the market consensus for the upcoming MJP settlement at USD 280-290/t and reports that traders in South Korea and Thailand have already repriced offers toward that band. Producers including Rio Tinto and South32 opened at $310-325/t on 02-September against a Q3 record of $395. A settlement at $285 would be a fall of roughly 28% in one quarter and would require producers to concede a further $20-30/t from their opening offer. This page has narrowed its pending range to $280-310 - the first change in nine runs, and the first made on new evidence rather than judgement.

OVERSEAS PHYSICAL PREMIUMS ARE SOFT ACROSS EVERY REGION SMM SURVEYS, AND THE DETAIL CONTRADICTS THE GULF-SCARCITY NARRATIVE THAT SUPPORTS THE LONDON CURVE. Japan's spot premiums fell again on deteriorating end-user demand with restocking limited to immediate needs; the US saw only scattered deals with premiums under pressure and no sign of stabilization; Vietnam was depressed with almost no genuine large-volume trades; Korea and Thailand are repricing toward the lower MJP band. Most pointedly, SMM describes primary ingot supply from the MIDDLE EAST AND AUSTRALIA into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE. The physical Asian market is not behaving as though Middle East metal is scarce, and that is the single most important piece of counter-evidence on this page.

LME ALUMINIUM STOCK MOVED FOR THE FIRST TIME IN FOUR READINGS, FALLING 175 TONNES TO 244,350 - A FRESH SERIES LOW AND A TOKEN DRAW AT THE SAME TIME. The four-session standstill at 244,525 is broken, which matters because a market being drained does not print the same tonne four times running. But 175 tonnes is seven hundredths of one percent of the stock. Across the fifteen sessions to 10-September the series has fallen 2,575 tonnes, about 172 a session, and all but 175 of that happened before 04-September. On the same board lead drew 2,075 tonnes and zinc 4,325. The level remains a floor under the price; the flow is still not a trigger.

THE CONFLICT ESCALATED ON TWO FRONTS AND OPENED A SECOND CHOKEPOINT. Iran said it attacked ten ships near the Strait of Hormuz and the United States said it retaliated by sinking five Iranian tankers, the worst fighting in months as the war nears seven months. Separately the Houthi group was reported to have seized the port city of Mocha, gaining leverage over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, declaring a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia and striking Saudi energy infrastructure. Brent traded as high as $109.97, its highest since early May, and was up roughly 12.4% on the week. A Bab el-Mandeb disruption would close an alternative routing that Hormuz-affected cargo has partly relied on.

THE FIRST DE-ESCALATION SIGNAL IN MONTHS APPEARED LATE IN THE SESSION AND IT IS UNCONFIRMED. A later headline on the same publisher's dispatch reported oil REVERSING COURSE AND FALLING ABOUT 1% ON A REPORT THAT IRAN AND OMAN ARE SEEKING A HORMUZ DEAL. No dated primary announcement was retrievable at this compile, so it is carried as a developing report rather than an agreement, with a low confidence read attached. IT IS FLAGGED BECAUSE OF ITS ASYMMETRY RATHER THAN ITS PROBABILITY: the Gulf disruption is the largest single pillar of the bull case and the only one that could unwind in days rather than quarters. Anyone treating the Gulf outage as structural should watch this specific story.

US AUGUST PRODUCER PRICES CAME IN HOT ON THE ANNUAL RATE AND PUSHED SEPTEMBER FED HIKE ODDS TO ROUGHLY 70%. The index rose 0.4% month on month, in line, but 5.4% year on year, a tenth above expectations, with final-demand goods up 1.1%, energy up 4.2% and diesel alone up 24.1%. The ten-year yield pushed toward 4.93%, near the 5.00% handle; equities closed lower and gold fell about 2%. THE COMPOSITION IS A COST STORY AS WELL AS A POLICY STORY: energy and diesel inflation of that magnitude is freight and power cost arriving in the official data, which is exactly the line a smelter cannot hedge.

THE ECB RAISED RATES 25 BASIS POINTS UNANIMOUSLY AND LAGARDE CALLED IT A 'NO-BRAINER', BUT THE EURO FELL ANYWAY. The deposit rate went to 2.50%, the main refinancing rate to 2.65% and the marginal lending facility to 2.90% - the second rise since the Iran war began. The Council declined to pre-commit to a further step, yet faster inflation forecasts and an acknowledgement of euro-area resilience moved markets to price roughly 88 basis points more tightening with a peak in September 2027. FOR THIS INDUSTRY THE CONSEQUENCE IS NARROW AND NEGATIVE: European restart economics now face a rising policy rate and a gas price up roughly 11.5% in four sessions at the same time, three weeks before Slovalco's guided Q4 restart.

ALUMINA PRINTED ITS FIRST FRESH DATED TRADE IN FIVE WEEKS AND BARELY MOVED, WHICH IS A QUIET DISAPPOINTMENT TO THE FALLING-COST THESIS. SMM reports 50,000 mt traded at $353.50/mt FOB East Australia for October shipment on 11-September, against $356/t on the identical basis on 05-August - down $2.50, or 0.7%, across five weeks in which published commentary repeatedly guided that September prices would fall on surplus and inventory buildup. At roughly two tonnes of alumina per tonne of metal that is worth about $5 a tonne of aluminium, against an energy tape that moved multiples of that in the same window. A second trade the same day at $373/mt FOB Indonesia for November shipment is noted separately and not mixed into the Australian series.

ALCOA CUT ITS 2026 ALUMINA PRODUCTION GUIDANCE BY 200,000-300,000 TONNES TO 9.5-9.6 MILLION TONNES AFTER OPERATIONAL DISRUPTIONS. That is a genuine reduction in refinery output from a top-tier producer and it cuts against the surplus-alumina consensus this page has carried for weeks. It sits awkwardly beside the 11-September FOB East Australia trade, which showed almost no price response, and the awkwardness is left visible rather than resolved by assertion: either the surplus is large enough to absorb the cut, or the price has not yet reflected it.

BAUXITE INVENTORY AT TEN CHINESE PORTS FELL 1,610,000 TONNES IN A SINGLE WEEK, ACCORDING TO SMM'S PORT SURVEY OF 11-SEPTEMBER. Bauxite is the least-watched and most geographically concentrated link in this chain, with Guinea supply the recurring driver of Pacific alumina strength. Because roughly two tonnes of alumina are needed per tonne of metal, and two to three tonnes of bauxite per tonne of alumina, a disruption here propagates with a lag rather than immediately. The draw is consistent with refineries running high operating rates rather than contradicting the surplus view - but it thins the buffer if Guinea supply is interrupted.

EGA AND ALBA BOTH SOUNDED CONSTRUCTIVE ON RECOVERY AND PUBLIC REPORTING ATTRIBUTED THE SESSION'S WEAKNESS DIRECTLY TO IT. EGA stated Al Taweelah is operating at 18% of capacity and expects to return to previous output levels in EARLY 2027 - a firmer calendar than this page previously carried. GCC primary output was down 44% year on year in July at 293,000 tonnes against 523,000, and global primary production fell 1.7% year on year to 6.16 million tonnes. THE DISTINCTION THIS PAGE HAS DRAWN BETWEEN SCHEDULED RESTARTS AND UNDATED OUTAGES IS NARROWING: Alba's lines remain idled with no published schedule, but the company is no longer silent about returning.

THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

earnings.note: BACK-FILLED INTO THE PER-COMPANY HISTORY PANEL THIS RUN WITH FOUR SOURCED QUARTERS OF ADJUSTED EBITDA. Q1 FY27 (three months to 30-June-2026): net income $164m, up 71% year on year; ADJUSTED EBITDA $516m, UP 24% year on year; adjusted EBITDA per tonne shipped $563, up 30% year on year; net sales $5.8bn. The prior three quarters were $459m in Q4 FY26 (down 3% y/y, $544/t), $348m in Q3 FY26 (down 5% y/y, $430/t) and $422m in Q2 FY26 (down 9% y/y, $448/t) - all three depressed by the Oswego fires of September and November 2025 and by tariff headwinds. THE FOUR-QUARTER SERIES IS THE POINT AND IT IS WHY THIS COMPANY WAS CHOSEN FOR THIS RUN'S BACKFILL: it is the cleanest public evidence available of how a downstream converter recovers from an operational shock, and of what the 2026 premium environment has been worth to the downstream. Adjusted EBITDA fell for three consecutive quarters - $422m, $348m, $459m - and then stepped up 12.4% sequentially and 24% year on year to $516m in the June quarter. THE PER-TONNE LINE IS THE MORE INFORMATIVE OF THE TWO because it strips shipment volume out: $448, $430, $544, $563. That is a 31% improvement in unit conversion economics across four quarters in a business whose metal cost is passed through. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE IS AS IMPORTANT AS WHAT IT DOES: a converter's EBITDA per tonne rising through a period of record US premiums is consistent with the premium being captured downstream, but Novelis does not publish a split between recovered metal-price spread, recycling spread and true conversion pricing, so this page does not claim one. THE GENERIC READ-ACROSS IS THAT THE DOWNSTREAM SIDE OF THE CHAIN ENTERED THE SECOND HALF OF 2026 WITH MOMENTUM, which is consistent with Constellium and Kaiser on the same panel and with the stable $727.50 Rotterdam billet conversion spread on the premium panel.

earnings.note: BACKFILLED INTO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A FULL FOUR-QUARTER SOURCED HISTORY. Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

earnings.note: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER, AND THE THIRD IN A ROW. Press Metal Aluminium reported net profit of MYR 624.5m for the quarter ended 31-March-2026, UP 35.2% year-on-year from MYR 461.77m, on revenue of MYR 4.1bn (+5.2%). The company attributed the result to stronger aluminium prices, higher sales volumes and LOWER INPUT COSTS - the same three forces visible in every other producer on this panel. ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN as the tenth company in the earnings_history series. THE PERIOD IS DELIBERATELY OLDER THAN THE REST OF THE PANEL AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: Press Metal's Q2-2026 result had not published publicly at this compile and is expected in late August. WHY IT WAS WORTH ADDING: Press Metal is the largest primary aluminium producer in South-East Asia and the panel was otherwise weighted to Western, Indian, Gulf and Chinese producers. It is a hydro-powered, non-Chinese, non-Gulf smelter - which makes it the cleanest available control on the question of whether the margin expansion running through this panel is genuinely driven by the metal price and the cheap alumina leg, or by region-specific factors like Section 232 protection or Gulf supply disruption. A 35% profit increase at a producer with no exposure to either strongly supports the former. ITS Q2 RESULT IN LATE AUGUST IS THE MORE INTERESTING DATAPOINT, because it will cover the quarter in which alumina fell to roughly 10.7% of the metal price.

trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE RATHER THAN REFRESHED DAILY. THEY ARE RE-RATED THIS RUN AND THE TRIGGER IS SPECIFIC AND DATED: CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS TAKE EFFECT TODAY, 08-SEPTEMBER-2026, AND EXPLICITLY INCLUDE ALUMINIUM. Canada is applying 15%, 25% and 50% tariffs on products drawn from those targeted by the US Section 338 and Section 232 measures, with each product's rate matched to the corresponding US rate; IN STEEL AND ALUMINIUM THE EXISTING 25% COUNTER-TARIFF RISES TO 50%. The package covers $27.6 billion of US imports and more than 300 metals products and derivatives including flat-rolled steel and aluminium bars, and is described by the Canadian government as matching the US Section 338 tariffs dollar for dollar after the US imposed 50% on $27.6 billion of Canadian goods effective 22-August. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL TARIFF HEADLINE: the Canada-United States corridor is by volume the most important primary-aluminium trade route in the world, and it is now taxed in BOTH directions rather than one. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR A PHYSICAL READER IS DECOUPLING RATHER THAN SIMPLE INFLATION - regional delivered premiums on both sides of the border are mechanically supported because arbitrage between them is more expensive, while the volume that actually crosses is suppressed, so the delivered price and the exchange benchmark drift further apart. THE SECOND ACTIVE DRIVER IS UNCHANGED AND STILL UNRESOLVED: the latest escalation in US-Iran hostilities has raised uncertainty over any return of Persian Gulf supply, and Middle East LNG scarcity on tanker disruption continues to constrain regional refining and smelting.

flows.note: Semi-finished exports 3.2 Mt in January-June, +18% year on year, with June at a record 695,000 t. catalysts.text: US AUGUST CONSUMER PRICES - TODAY. THE SEQUENCING IS THE POINT: producer prices already surprised to the upside yesterday at 5.4% year on year, a tenth above expectations, and lifted September Fed hike odds to roughly 70%. CPI therefore arrives with the market already leaning hawkish and with only three sessions before the Federal Reserve decides. Published previews expect the headline to COOL, which makes the asymmetry unusually sharp: an in-line or hotter print leaves a rise close to fully priced, while a genuine downside surprise has more room to move yields than an upside one does. Direct read-through to a dollar-priced metal through both the dollar and the discount rate.

US FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION - THREE SESSIONS AWAY AND THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL SINGLE DATE ON THIS PAGE. August payrolls printed +162,000 against a consensus near 53,000 with prior months revised up a combined 55,000, and the hot producer-price print pushed implied odds of a HIKE to roughly 70% from about 61%. THE OPEN QUESTION HAS FULLY FLIPPED FROM WHETHER THE FED CUTS TO WHETHER IT RAISES. Direct headwind for a dollar-priced metal; simultaneously a brake on the restart pipeline through the discount rate, so the net effect on the physical balance is ambiguous even where the effect on price is not. THE COUNTER-OBSERVATION THIS PAGE CARRIED FOR THREE SESSIONS HAS BEEN WITHDRAWN: the metal fell with everything else on 10-September.

RESOLUTION OF THE OCTOBER-DECEMBER ASIAN QUARTERLY PREMIUM, NOW WITH A DATED CONSENSUS NUMBER FOR THE FIRST TIME. SMM's 11-September review puts the market consensus at USD 280-290/t and reports Korean and Thai traders already repricing toward that band. Producers including Rio Tinto and South32 opened at $310-325/t on 02-September against the Q3 record of $395, with buyers targeting below $300. THE CONSENSUS NOW SITS BELOW THE PRODUCERS' OWN OFFER FLOOR, so the burden of concession has moved to the sellers. This page has narrowed its pending range to $280-310, the first change in nine runs and the first made on evidence rather than judgement. IF IT SETTLES NEAR $280-290 WHILE LONDON IS IN ITS WIDEST BACKWARDATION SINCE EARLY AUGUST, that is the strongest available evidence that physical Asia is materially looser than the exchange curve implies.

WHETHER THE BACKWARDATION HOLDS NOW THAT IT HAS WIDENED AGAINST THE PRICE - THIS IS THE CLEANEST TEST ON THE PAGE AND IT IS NEWLY WELL-POSED. The spread has widened on FOUR consecutive sessions, from a $0.50 contango through $2.00, $6.00 and $14.00 to $25.00, and on 10-September it widened while the flat price FELL, which closes off the momentum explanation. THE CONFIRMING OUTCOME IS THE SPREAD HOLDING ABOVE $14.00 THROUGH A SOFT PHYSICAL TAPE AND A HAWKISH FED; that would establish a location-specific tightness in London-deliverable metal. THE FALSIFYING OUTCOME IS EQUALLY CLEAR: the spread collapsing back inside $2.00 when the Japanese premium settles near $280 would mark the entire four-session sequence as positioning. Watch also whether the inventory pulse that resumed at 175 tonnes becomes a draw of meaningful size.

THE MIDDLE EAST, WHICH NOW HAS TWO CHOKEPOINTS AND ONE UNCONFIRMED OFF-RAMP. Iran attacked ten ships near the Strait of Hormuz and the US sank five Iranian tankers in retaliation; the Houthi group was reported to have seized Mocha, gaining leverage over BAB EL-MANDEB, declaring a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia and striking Saudi energy infrastructure. Brent traded as high as $109.97, up roughly 12.4% on the week. AGAINST THAT, A LATE AND UNCONFIRMED REPORT THAT IRAN AND OMAN ARE SEEKING A HORMUZ DEAL SENT OIL BACK ABOUT 1%. It is a single headline on a developing story and should be treated as unresolved until a dated primary announcement exists - but it is the one item on this page capable of unwinding the largest pillar of the bull case in days rather than quarters.

THE MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT CYCLE, NOW ABOUT FOUR SESSIONS AWAY, AND IT LANDS INTO A RISING ENERGY TAPE. Prebaked anode and coal tar pitch settle monthly on this cadence; the September anode settlement is public at 5,730 RMB/t spot and 5,745 RMB/t acceptance, above August's 5,630, and coal tar pitch has not printed a newer mark since 13-August. SMM expects September anode and aluminium fluoride both to RISE. THE COMFORTABLE READING THAT FALLING ALUMINA MEANS FALLING CASH COST IS NOW EXPLICITLY UNSUPPORTED: alumina's first fresh dated trade in five weeks fell only $2.50, worth about $5 a tonne of metal, while Brent touched $109.97 and European gas rose roughly 11.5% across four sessions. A regional East China anode spot quotation of RMB 5,230/t remains visible and is deliberately NOT appended, because mixing a regional spot basis into a national settlement series would corrupt the trend rather than extend it.

THE FIRST MEASURABLE TEST OF CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS, WHICH TOOK EFFECT 08-SEPTEMBER AND RAISED CANADIAN COUNTER-TARIFFS ON US STEEL AND ALUMINIUM FROM 25% TO 50%. THREE FULL DAYS IN, THE ONLY DATED PUBLIC EVIDENCE POINTS AGAINST THE MECHANICAL EXPECTATION: SMM reports only scattered US spot deals, spot prices extending losses, regional premiums under pressure and no clear sign of stabilization. Because premium assessments are periodic rather than daily, the measurable effect still awaits a dated assessment, and nothing has been written into the premium rows on the strength of either the policy or the commentary. The US Midwest duty-paid row is carried at $2,094/t, of which $1,671.50 is the arithmetic tariff leg at a verified 50% rate on the $3,343.00 benchmark, leaving an implied market leg of $422.50 - up $4.50 purely because the benchmark FELL while the assessment stood still.

THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT - roughly fifteen weeks away. The European duty-unpaid premium is the price that must absorb it, and at a last assessment of $485/t, below its own trailing average of $519.10 and against dated commentary describing overseas premiums as broadly soft, it is not behaving as though the event is coming. Either replacement units are already sourced or the event is not priced; the assessment cadence is too slow to tell which. THE PRESSURE ON THE REPLACEMENT-SUPPLY SIDE INCREASED AGAIN, with European gas up roughly 11.5% across four sessions and the ECB tightening on 10-September with about 88 basis points more priced. Slovalco's Q4-2026 start is roughly three weeks away and is the nearest European addition standing in that squeeze.

risks.text: RE-ASSESSED 11-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT FLAT, AND THE FIRST DATED EVIDENCE SINCE THE MEASURE TOOK EFFECT ARGUES AGAINST THE RISK RATHER THAN FOR IT. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT TARIFF POLICY, NOT SUPPLY AND DEMAND, BECOMES THE DOMINANT DETERMINANT OF REGIONAL DELIVERED PRICE. Canada's counter-tariffs have been in force since 08-September at 50%, matching a US Section 232 rate re-verified this run at 50% on articles and 25% on derivatives, across $27.6 billion of imports and more than 300 metals products. Neither government has announced further escalation. THE MECHANICAL EXPECTATION WAS SUPPORT FOR DELIVERED PREMIUMS ON BOTH SIDES OF A CORRIDOR WHOSE VOLUME IS SUPPRESSED. THREE FULL DAYS IN, SMM'S 11-SEPTEMBER REVIEW REPORTS THE OPPOSITE: only scattered US spot deals, lacklustre downstream consumption on the seasonal off-season, spot prices extending losses, regional premiums under pressure and NO CLEAR SIGN OF STABILIZATION. DEMAND IS CURRENTLY BEATING POLICY, AND THAT IS THE FIRST REAL TEST THIS RISK HAS FAILED. It is held at FLAT rather than lowered because one weekly commentary is not a dated assessment, the level of the risk remains HIGH, and the incremental risk from here is further escalation by either party - a separate and currently unsignalled event. Nothing has been written into the premium rows on the strength of the policy.

RE-ASSESSED 11-SEPTEMBER. RAISED FROM FLAT TO UP, AND THE REASON IS A DATED CALENDAR RATHER THAN A CHANGE IN TONE. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT CURTAILED AND DISRUPTED CAPACITY RETURNS FASTER THAN THE MARKET EXPECTS. TWO THINGS CHANGED TOGETHER TODAY AND BOTH ARE PUBLIC STATEMENTS BY THE OPERATORS THEMSELVES. EGA SAID AL TAWEELAH IS OPERATING AT 18% OF CAPACITY AND EXPECTS TO RETURN TO PREVIOUS OUTPUT LEVELS IN EARLY 2027 - a firmer calendar than this page previously carried, alongside a lower current run-rate. AND ALBA'S RAMP-UP EXPECTATIONS WERE PUBLICLY DESCRIBED AS UPBEAT, which narrows the distinction this page has drawn between scheduled restarts and undated outages; Alba's lines 1-3 remain idled with no published schedule, but the company is no longer silent about returning. Public reporting attributed the session's aluminium weakness directly to both. THE EXISTING PIPELINE IS UNCHANGED AND ALREADY LONG: Slovalco's first 75,000 t of 175,000 guided to Q4-2026, roughly three weeks away; Alcoa's San Ciprian close to full on energy hedged through 2027 and Portland's 15,000 t completed in Q2-2026; Century's Mt Holly at full capacity for the first time since 2015 on a $50m investment; and Magnitude 7 Metals' Missouri potline guided before end-2026 at ~75,000 t. THE GATING CONDITION DID WORSEN AGAIN AND IS REPORTED FOR BALANCE: European gas rose a fourth consecutive session to EUR 81.57, up roughly 11.5% across those sessions, and the US ten-year pushed toward 4.93% on a hot producer-price print, so the operating cost and the hurdle rate of the next restart decision both rose. THAT OFFSET IS REAL BUT IT IS WEAKER THAN A DATED GUIDANCE STATEMENT FROM THE OPERATOR OF THE LARGEST DISRUPTED ASSET, which is why the trend is raised.

RE-ASSESSED 11-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP, AND THE SINGLE PIECE OF COUNTER-EVIDENCE THIS PAGE HAS LEANED ON FOR THREE SESSIONS HAS BEEN WITHDRAWN. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT MACRO TIGHTENING OVERWHELMS THE PHYSICAL STORY. US AUGUST PRODUCER PRICES ROSE 0.4% MONTH ON MONTH, IN LINE, BUT 5.4% YEAR ON YEAR, A TENTH ABOVE EXPECTATIONS, with final-demand goods up 1.1%, energy up 4.2% and diesel alone up 24.1%. Market-implied odds of a September Federal Reserve RISE moved to roughly 70% from about 61% earlier in the week; the ten-year pushed toward 4.93%, near the 5.00% handle; the dollar firmed; equities fell and gold dropped about 2%. THE ECB RAISED ITS THREE KEY RATES 25 BASIS POINTS UNANIMOUSLY on 10-September to a 2.50% deposit rate, with Lagarde calling it a 'no-brainer' and markets pricing roughly 88 basis points more tightening peaking in September 2027. TWO MAJOR CENTRAL BANKS ARE NOW TIGHTENING OR EXPECTED TO TIGHTEN INTO THE SAME QUARTER. FOR THREE SESSIONS THIS PAGE NOTED THAT ALUMINIUM ROSE ANYWAY AND TREATED THAT AS EVIDENCE THAT THE PHYSICAL BID COULD OVERCOME THE MACRO. TODAY IT DID NOT RISE - it fell 0.60% on the three-month with every other base metal - SO THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE IS WITHDRAWN EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED. THE ONE REMAINING MITIGANT IS STRUCTURAL AND IS STATED WITH ITS LIMIT: a higher discount rate is also a brake on every restart and expansion decision in the supply pipeline, so the net effect on the physical balance is ambiguous even where the effect on price is not. US August consumer prices land today and the Fed decides in three sessions.

RE-ASSESSED 11-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP AND IT ESCALATED ON TWO FRONTS RATHER THAN ONE - BUT FOR THE FIRST TIME IN MONTHS A DE-ESCALATION SIGNAL ALSO APPEARED, AND BOTH ARE REPORTED. THE ESCALATION IS DATED AND SPECIFIC: Iran said it attacked TEN SHIPS near the Strait of Hormuz and the United States said it retaliated by SINKING FIVE IRANIAN TANKERS, the worst fighting in months as the conflict nears seven months. SEPARATELY, THE HOUTHI GROUP WAS REPORTED TO HAVE SEIZED THE PORT CITY OF MOCHA, gaining leverage over the BAB EL-MANDEB STRAIT, declaring a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia and striking Saudi energy infrastructure. A SECOND CHOKEPOINT IS NOW IN PLAY, which would close an alternative routing that Hormuz-affected cargo has partly relied on. Brent traded as high as $109.97, its highest since early May, up roughly 12.4% on the week. THE UNDERLYING CAPACITY LOSS REMAINS OBSERVABLE IN PUBLIC DISCLOSURE RATHER THAN INFERRED: Qatalum at roughly 60% of a 648,000-tonne nameplate on reduced gas with a force majeure outstanding and no resolution date, Alba's lines 1-3 idled since March 2026, and GCC primary output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000. THE DE-ESCALATION SIGNAL IS CARRIED WITH LOW CONFIDENCE AND IS NOT ALLOWED TO CHANGE THE TREND: a late headline reported oil reversing about 1% on a report that IRAN AND OMAN ARE SEEKING A HORMUZ DEAL. No dated primary announcement was retrievable. It is flagged for its ASYMMETRY rather than its probability - it is the only item on this page that could unwind the largest pillar of the bull case in days. THE CONTRADICTION THAT KEEPS THIS HONEST IS ON THE PHYSICAL SIDE: SMM describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE. Gulf output is demonstrably down 44% and Gulf metal is nonetheless reaching Asia in quantity. Both are true and the page does not force them to agree.

RE-ASSESSED 11-SEPTEMBER. LOWERED FROM UP TO FLAT, AND THIS IS A DELIBERATE RE-RATING ON A PRINT RATHER THAN ON A MOOD. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK PROPAGATING INTO SMELTER MARGIN. THE ROW HAD BEEN STALE FOR FIVE WEEKS AND THE STALENESS IS NOW GONE: SMM reports 50,000 mt traded at $353.50/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA for October shipment on 11-September, against $356/t on the IDENTICAL basis on 05-August. The feared shock did not arrive; the price fell $2.50, or 0.7%. At roughly two tonnes of alumina per tonne of metal that is worth about $5 a tonne of aluminium. THE REASON IT IS LOWERED TO FLAT RATHER THAN TO DOWN IS THAT TWO SUPPLY-SIDE FACTS PULL THE OTHER WAY AND THEY ARE NOT SMALL. ALCOA CUT ITS 2026 ALUMINA PRODUCTION GUIDANCE BY 200,000-300,000 TONNES TO 9.5-9.6 MILLION TONNES after operational disruptions - a genuine reduction from a top-tier refiner that cuts against the surplus consensus this page has carried for weeks. AND BAUXITE INVENTORY AT TEN CHINESE PORTS FELL 1,610,000 TONNES IN A SINGLE WEEK, the raw material one step further upstream drawing hard. ALUNORTE REMAINS THE STRUCTURAL FRAGILITY AND THE WORD TEMPORARY REMAINS LOAD-BEARING: the world's largest alumina refinery outside China is back at full capacity on a TEMPORARY terminal-access agreement with its gas supplier, and European gas rose a fourth consecutive session with Brent touching $109.97. A temporary gas accommodation is harder to renew in a tightening gas market than in a loosening one. THE HONEST SUMMARY IS THAT THE ALUMINA HEADLINE IS BENIGN, THE ALUMINA SUPPLY NEWS IS NOT, AND THE COST STACK OVERALL IS STILL RISING BECAUSE ENERGY DOMINATES IT.

RE-ASSESSED 11-SEPTEMBER. RAISED FROM FLAT TO UP, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE STALENESS ARGUMENT THAT HAS HELD THIS RISK DOWN FOR SEVERAL RUNS NO LONGER EXISTS. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT CHINESE EXPORT SUPPLY RELIEVES THE WESTERN SHORTAGE FASTER THAN THE BALANCE FORECASTS ASSUME. FRESH DATA PRINTED: CHINA'S AUGUST ALUMINIUM EXPORTS WERE 626,000 TONNES, TAKING JANUARY-AUGUST EXPORTS TO 4.67 MILLION TONNES, UP 16.7% YEAR ON YEAR. The page previously carried only a July figure of +18.7% year on year and explicitly flagged that carrying it further would be drift rather than evidence. THE TWO FIGURES ARE NOT LIKE FOR LIKE - one is a single-month year-on-year rate, the other a cumulative eight-month rate - SO NO DECELERATION IS INFERRED FROM THE DIFFERENCE AND NONE IS CLAIMED. THE CORROBORATING EVIDENCE IS WHAT MAKES THIS AN UPGRADE RATHER THAN A REFRESH, AND IT IS ALL DATED TODAY. SMM describes Asian premiums soft across five regions with the Q4 Japanese consensus at $280-290 against $395 settled; Japanese port inventories fell 8.8% month on month to 201,000 tonnes; and Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan is described as RELATIVELY AMPLE. ABUNDANT REGIONAL SUPPLY AND COLLAPSING REGIONAL PREMIUMS ARE EXACTLY WHAT THIS RISK PREDICTS. THE MECHANISM STILL MATTERS MORE THAN THE NUMBER: the relieving metal arrives as semi-finished and alloy product that does not pass through LME warehouses, which is one coherent explanation for how a multi-decade exchange inventory low can coexist with a warehouse series that barely moves. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS UNCHANGED AND IS NOT DISMISSED: if ample Chinese and Gulf metal were satisfying Western prompt demand, the front of the aluminium curve should not have widened its backwardation on a FALLING price. The export flow explains the flat inventory and the soft premiums; it does not explain the tightening curve.

RE-ASSESSED 11-SEPTEMBER. LOWERED FROM UP TO FLAT, ON A 175-TONNE FACT, AND THE SMALLNESS OF THAT FACT IS ACKNOWLEDGED IN THE SAME BREATH AS THE RE-RATING. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT THE INVENTORY ARGUMENT UNDERPINNING THE BULL CASE STOPS WORKING. EXCHANGE STOCK FELL 175 TONNES TO 244,350 ON 10-SEPTEMBER - THE FIRST NON-ZERO PUBLISHED CHANGE IN THREE SESSIONS AND THE FIRST NEW NUMBER IN FOUR READINGS, and a fresh low for the series at what public commentary describes as a thirty-six-year low. The statement this page has made for four runs - that level and flow have FULLY separated - is no longer strictly true, and it is corrected rather than repeated. THE SIZE IS STATED HONESTLY: 175 tonnes is seven hundredths of one percent of the stock. On the same board lead drew 2,075 tonnes and zinc 4,325. Aluminium has the lowest relative inventory of the five metals and the smallest draw. THIS IS A SERIES RESUMING A PULSE, NOT A WAREHOUSE BEING DRAINED, and the trend is lowered to flat rather than to down for exactly that reason. ACROSS THE FIFTEEN SESSIONS TO 10-SEPTEMBER STOCK HAS FALLEN 2,575 TONNES, ABOUT 172 A SESSION, AND ALL BUT 175 OF THAT HAPPENED BEFORE 04-SEPTEMBER. THE OFF-EXCHANGE SERIES CONTINUE TO DISAGREE WITH LONDON AND ARE REPORTED FOR BALANCE: Japanese inventories at three major ports fell 8.8% month on month to 201,000 tonnes and Shanghai stocks fell 3% week on week. THE PRACTICAL READ IS UNCHANGED: treat the inventory statistic as a floor under the price rather than as a trigger for the next leg higher.

RE-ASSESSED 11-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP. THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT 31-DECEMBER-2026 AND IS THE LARGEST SCHEDULED STRUCTURAL EVENT ON THIS PAGE - now roughly fifteen weeks away. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS A DISORDERLY EUROPEAN SUPPLY RESET. THE EUROPEAN DUTY-UNPAID PREMIUM IS THE PRICE THAT MUST ABSORB IT AND IT IS STILL NOT BEHAVING AS IF THE EVENT IS COMING: last assessed at $485/t, BELOW its own trailing average of $519.10. THE SUPPORTING EVIDENCE FOR SOFTNESS GREW RATHER THAN SHRANK THIS RUN - SMM's 11-September review describes overseas premiums as broadly soft across five regions with demand unlikely to improve materially in the short run. TWO READINGS REMAIN LIVE AND THE ASSESSMENT CADENCE IS TOO SLOW TO DISTINGUISH THEM: either replacement units are already sourced and the ban is priced, or the event is not in the price at all. The second reading is the risk and it becomes harder to hedge the closer the date comes. THE SECOND-ORDER PRESSURE INCREASED AGAIN ON BOTH HALVES AT ONCE. European gas TTF rose a fourth consecutive session to EUR 81.57, roughly 11.5% across those sessions, and the European Central Bank raised rates 25 basis points on 10-September with markets pricing about 88 basis points more to come. THE REGION THAT MUST ABSORB A SUPPLY SHOCK AT YEAR END FACES A RISING ENERGY COST AND A RISING POLICY RATE SIMULTANEOUSLY, which narrows the room for European restarts to supply the replacement units. Slovalco's Q4-2026 restart, roughly three weeks away, is the nearest European addition and sits directly in that squeeze.

A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
